title: Stop the search
intro: The search pattern walks the array and returns the moment it finds its target. It returns -1 only once every box has said no. You are the search.

rounds.right: Found at index {result} after {comparisons} comparisons: `return` ended the loop the moment it matched, so the boxes after it were never looked at.

why.notMatch: `{value}.equals({target})` is `false`: not this one, so the loop keeps walking.
why.missed: `{value}.equals({target})` is `true`, so the search returns `i` right here, without looking any further.
why.early: `-1` means every box said no, but the boxes from index {i} to {last} haven't been checked yet.
why.end: `i` is {length}, and `{length} < {length}` is false: the loop is over.

rounds.right: All {length} boxes said no: {comparisons} comparisons, and only then `return -1`. No index is ever -1, which is why it can mean "not found".

why.notMatch: `{value}.equals({target})` is `false`: not this one, so the loop keeps walking.
why.missed: `{value}.equals({target})` is `true`, so the search returns `i` right here.
why.early: Not yet: `-1` means every box said no, and the boxes from index {i} to {last} haven't been checked.
why.end: `i` is {length}, and `{length} < {length}` is false: the loop is over and nothing matched. Only one line is left to run.

rounds.prompt: This time {target} is in `{name}` twice. You are `find({name}, {target})`: stop at the right moment.
rounds.right: `return {result}`: the first match wins, because `return` ends the loop right there. The second {target} further along is never looked at.

why.notMatch: `{value}.equals({target})` is `false`: not this one, so the loop keeps walking.
why.missed: `{value}.equals({target})` is `true`, so the search returns `i` right here. It never gets as far as the second one.
why.early: `-1` means every box said no, but the boxes from index {i} to {last} haven't been checked yet.
why.end: `i` is {length}, and `{length} < {length}` is false: the loop is over.
